headline: Record banking and equities offset weak fixed income
summary_short: Jefferies Q3 net revenues were $2,222M (+8.5% y/y) and diluted EPS was $1.08 versus $1.01 a year earlier, on record investment banking and equities.
summary_long: Net revenues rose 8.5% y/y to $2,222M. Investment banking reached $1,331M (+17%) with record Advisory at $818M, and Equities hit a record $626M (+29%). Fixed income fell 26% to $176M on low industry volumes, and Asset Management net revenues dropped to $86M from $177M. Compensation ratio was 53.7% versus 52.9%. The company repurchased $70M of stock, declared a $0.40 quarterly dividend, and restored its buyback authorization to $250M.
confidence_notes: Figures come from the press release (in thousands, rounded here). The shard's q/q reference for EPS points to FY2026 Q1 and its y/y is basic EPS, so EPS deltas use the release's own diluted-per-voting-share comparison (y/y only). Return on adjusted tangible equity is a non-GAAP, annualized measure. Voting and non-voting common shares carry different EPS after SMBC's preferred conversion.

drivers.explanation: Record Advisory (+25%) on market share gains and strong sponsor-led M&A in healthcare, industrials and energy; equity underwriting up 69%.
Lower industry volumes and ongoing slowness in market activity.
Preferred dividends fell to $6M from $29M a year ago as SMBC converted preferred shares, alongside higher banking and equities revenue.
Management points to record Investment Banking and Equities, offset by a subdued Fixed Income market and weaker fund performance in Asset Management.
